key_insight: Lyapunov-Liouville closures can reproduce the full decay and small-scale statistics of freely decaying isotropic turbulence across velocity and scalar fields, including regime-dependent intermittency and scaling laws.
engineering_relevance: The results support reduced-order turbulence and scalar-mixing models for predicting decay rates, characteristic length scales, and high-Pr transport behavior in engineering flows.
method: Integrate closed von Kármán–Howarth and Corrsin equations with a high-accuracy autonomous solver
Test three initial correlation families: Saffman-Birkhoff, Loitsiansky, and Gaussian
Compare decay exponents, microscale evolution, and increment PDFs across Pr = 10^-3 to 1000
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical validation over three initial states and a wide Prandtl-number range, with matched asymptotic exponents, Batchelor/Obukhov-Corrsin constants, and PDFs spanning quasi-Gaussian to intermittent behavior.
watch_item: The Gaussian initial condition reaches an operational limit by t = 33 when R_lambda falls below 10, so applicability may be constrained at very low Reynolds numbers or late-time strong decay.
paper_title: Numerical Validation of Lyapunov-Liouville Theory and Non-Diffusive Closures in Decaying Isotropic Fluid and Scalar Turbulence
